items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: And, see, Joe Turner would say shuffle in G, and he would get to singing in the key of G.

ctx.x: Now that was a- I wanted to know what that meant.

Well, that just was a, Monkey Man, what it mean is that I, in essence, I ain't going to be your fool no more. Oh. That's all. And, see, this was a, like back then, Joe Turner, you know, that's called a, you walk on a bandstand and they play the shuffle and B flat, and I could sing Monkey Man. Right. Yeah, you know, or either any one of Joe Turner songs, you know, back then, because that's just a shuffle. Yeah. And, see, Joe Turner would say shuffle in G, and he would get to singing in the key of G. And Joe Turner…
Oh, many, many, many, many, many, many times.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: Like with Joe, like as an example with Joe Turner. Joe Turner would just, find his key, and you know where he was

ctx.x: Okay, well, let's, um, I don't know if we could just stop there. I had, for now, um, there was something about the Dendler, a short question on the Doudrop back here. When you had a singer, a new singer came into town that you had to back up, would there, would you have a rehearsal with her?

Yeah, well, either we'd have a rehearsal or we knew that particular singer's songs that they would do. We would get a list of the songs that they would do, or they hit record, they had a hit record, we learned a hit record, and just go from there. You know, because for some reason the music was a little bit easier then than it is now. The music is a little more complicated because of the new chord progression that they use today. And, uh, back then, you know, it was more or less a three chord thing, or either…
You mentioned Little Richard. What was Little Richard like?
